title: Feature‑anchored retainer backcalc
content:
Quick scratchpad — exploring a feature‑anchored retainer (FAR) model that ties a baseline monthly commitment to feature bundles (e.g., chat + embeddings + rerank) instead of pure token buckets. Notes, open questions, and rough maths.

Context / goal:
- Need a simple self‑serve retainer product: predictable revenue signal (MRR) for small to mid teams, easier onboarding than a custom dedicated contract.
- Keep UX friendly: single SKU (FAR Small / Medium / Large) that maps to a feature bundle and a throughput/latency envelope. Overage and bursts via credits.
- Offer explicit latency SLO uplift (low latency route) as a paid add‑on to capture value from latency‑sensitive apps.

Product sketch (customer facing):
- FAR Small $199/mo: chat (1 concurrent), embeddings (100k tokens), rerank 10k tokens, 10k burst credits, 30s SLO, basic telemetry
- FAR Medium $999/mo: chat (5 concurrent), embeddings (1M tokens), rerank 100k tokens, 100k burst credits, 10s SLO, advanced tracing
- FAR Large $3,999/mo: chat (20 concurrent), embeddings (5M tokens), rerank 500k tokens, 1M burst credits, 2s SLO, priority support
- Add‑ons: low‑latency lane (multiplier x1.5 on price), quantization help, private deployment advisory (one‑time fee)

High level econ assumptions (for backcalc):
- GPU amortized infra and SW costs attributable to inference: $3.50 / GPU‑hour (internal reserved price)
- Effective throughput for mixed workload (chat + embeddings + decode) = 200k tokens / GPU‑hour on avg (very rough; caching & batching reduce cost)
- Other infra + ops + margin overhead: 2x of GPU line (i.e., total fully loaded cost = GPU_cost * 3)
- Default target gross margin on FAR = 60%

Derivations (per 1M tokens):
- GPU hours per 1M tokens = 1,000,000 / 200,000 = 5 GPU‑hours
- Raw GPU cost = 5 * $3.50 = $17.50
- Fully loaded cost = 17.50 * 3 = $52.50 per 1M tokens
- To hit 60% gross margin, price per 1M tokens = 52.50 / (1‑0.60) = $131.25 (~$0.131 / 1k tokens)

Map to FAR SKUs (sanity check):
- FAR Small allocation (embeddings 100k + rerank 10k + chat baseline 50k = 160k tokens/mo) => cost = 0.16 * 131.25 = $21 -> covers infra easily; pricing tilt is for retainer/commitment revenue and concurrency reserve.
- FAR Medium allocation ~1.1M tokens => cost = 1.1 * 131.25 = $144 -> still well below $999 price (spread pays for concurrency, SLO uplift, and go‑to‑market).
- FAR Large allocation ~6M tokens => cost = 6 * 131.25 = $787.5 -> below $3,999 (again covers reserved capacity economics).

Where the rest of the price comes from:
- Concurrency reservation and tail‑latency guarantees: paying to hold reserved capacity that is idle frequently.
- Billing amortization for reserved GPU pools: we should treat the retainer as ~30–40% of the reserved capacity amortized (i.e., FAR customers subsidize a pool that sits idle much of the time).
- Support / SRE / account management for higher tiers.

Burst credit model (operational simplicity):
- Provide a monthly credit bucket (non‑transferable) that can be monetized as overages beyond allocation at a premium (e.g., 3x per‑unit price).
- Credits internal accounting: the cost of burst consumption should use spot GPU pricing (or billed at higher per‑token price) so high spikes don't break product margin.

Latency lane / SLO premium:
- Charge 1.5x on top of plan for low‑latency guarantee (2–10s depending on tier). Technically this maps to: higher priority routing + pre‑warmed KV caches + fractional reserved concurrency.
- Backcalc for 1.5x uplift: if baseline margin is 60%, reserving extra capacity for latency lane eats into utilization. Assume utilization penalty 30% (i.e., you need 30% more reserved capacity). If baseline reserved cost fraction is 0.4 of price, then price multiply = 1 / (1‑0.3*0.4) ~ 1.2; we price 1.5 as a convenience buffer and GTM simplifier.

Open questions / TODOs (research tasks):
- Validate 200k tokens/GPU‑hour number across representative models (gptx‑small, llama2‑13B, quantized 4bit). Need experiment matrix.
- How to represent cross‑feature usage: customers will shift tokens from embeddings -> chat; define soft pooling or strict per‑feature buckets?
- Role of KV caching: should FAR include prefix cache capacity as part of plan? If yes, this materially reduces cost for chat heavy apps (change token math).
- Credit decay and leftover bucket policy (rollover vs burn).
- Add meter for concurrency: how to translate "5 concurrent chat" into tokens and reserved GPU seconds.

Edge cases / heuristics for commercial team:
- If customer is chat‑heavy with <50ms tail requirements, recommend Dedicated or private with explicit commit; FAR should be positioned as low‑friction path to eventual Dedicated.
- Offer 1 month free buffer credits on first month to reduce activation friction.
- If a customer exceeds 3x the allocation for 2 consecutive months, trigger outreach and pricing review (sell migration to Dedicated).

Quick sensitivity checks:
- If GPU_cost doubles to $7/hr -> per 1M token fully loaded cost = (5*7)*3 = $105 -> price at 60% margin = 105 / 0.4 = $262.5 per 1M -> FAR Medium cost component doubles (~$288), still leaves room for retainer economics but reduces margin on reserved concurrency.
- If throughput is actually 400k tokens/GPU‑hour (better batching), cost per 1M tokens halves -> large upside for unit economics and we can lower overage price to be more competitive.

Notes on UX language to product copy (short):
- "FAR Small — predictable monthly access to chat, embeddings, and reranking with burst credits and optional low‑latency lane. No surprise token bills; pay more only when you burst."
- Keep docs with examples: "Your 10k burst credits = ~10M tokens at typical model mix" (we should calibrate example per model).

Action items (next few weeks):
- Run small benchmark: embed+chat+rerrank mixed trace on preferred infra to get tokens/GPU‑hour for small/medium/large models (Owner: Eli).
- Draft pricing page copy and FAQ for FAR (Owner: Rashmi).
- Build simple billing simulation notebook that maps real usage traces to FAR SKUs and shows GTM migration triggers (Owner: Jonah).

Random scribbles / heuristics I keep returning to:
- Cheap anchoring: charge ~3x the pure token‑based unit cost for small retainer: customers buy predictability and simplicity.
- Latency is monetizable — many apps prefer paying a lump instead of architecting around multiple fallback models.
- Simplicity > perfect granularity for SMB motion; enterprise buys Dedicated anyway.

Unresolved simplicity decisions:
- Pooling vs per‑feature buckets (pooling is friendlier but harder to guarantee SLOs).
- Whether to expose internal metric used for pricing (tokens/GPU‑hr) to customers.

End of scratchpad.

(quick tag line for the pricing page: "Feature‑anchored Retainers — predictable capacity, simple features, ready scale.")
